children.name: Stabiliser trim
children.definition: An event involving failure of the  system which controls the position and movement of the horizontal stabilizer/canard.

children.name: Flap/Flaperon - Trailing edge
children.definition: An event involving failure of the systems that controls the position and movement of the trailing edge flaps.

children.name: Yaw damper
children.definition: An event involving yaw damper malfuntion.

children.name: Aircraft operating in degraded flight control mode
children.definition: An event involving aircraft operating in a degraded flight control mode

children.name: Flight control computer
children.definition: Failure of one or more flight control computers.

children.name: 2800 Aircraft fuel system
children.definition: Safety report related to the aircraft fuel system which stores and delivers fuel to the engine. Includes engine driven fuel pumps for reciprocating engines, includes tanks (bladder), valves, boost pumps, etc., and those components which furnish a means of dumping fuel overboard.Includes integral and tip fuel tank leak detection and sealing. Does not include the structure of integral or tip fuel tanks and the fuel cell backing boards.

children.name: 2810 Fuel storage
children.definition: Safety report related to the fuel storage system which stores fuel. Includes tank sealing, bladder type cells, ventilating system, cell and tank inter-connectors, over wing filler necks and caps, etc. Also includes reservoir feed pumping systems and reservoirs within the tanks which are not part of the distribution system.

children.name: 2820 ACFT fuel distrib. system
children.definition: Safety report related to the aircraft fuel distribution system which is used to distribute fuel from the filler connector to the storage system and from the storage system to and including the power plant fuel quick disconnect. Includes items such as plumbing, pumps, valves, controls, etc.

children.name: 2830 Fuel dump system
children.definition: Safety report related to the Tfuel dump system which is used to dump fuel overboard during flight. Includes items such as plumbing, valves, controls, chutes, etc.

children.name: 2840 ACFT fuel indicating system
children.definition: Safety report related to the aircraft fuel indicating system which is used to indicate the quantity, temperature, and pressure of the fuel. Includes pressure warning systems for pumping systems within the tank, etc. Does not include engine fuel flow or pressure.

children.name: Fuel quantity indication
children.definition: A defect within the fuel quantity system which results in a fuel discrepancy

children.name: Fuel pressure
children.definition: A total or partial booster pump failure

children.name: Override/Jettison pump
children.definition: A total or partial failure of an override/jettison pump

children.name: Fuel crossfeed valve
children.definition: A failure of the valve or the ability to position the valve electrically

children.name: Fuel filter
children.definition: A defect with the filter, or after a blocked fuel filter warning has been received

children.name: Fuel jettison failure
children.definition: A defect within the system which prevents fuel from being jettisoned

children.name: Fuel leak
children.definition: A significant fuel leak observed pre-departure or during flight

children.name: Fuel valve
children.definition: A failure of a fuel valve other than a crossfeed valve

children.name: Fuel contamination
children.definition: Fuel contamination is suspected or confirmed

children.name: Fuel temperature
children.definition: The airframe or engine fuel temperature is outside of the normal operating range

children.name: 2900 Hydraulic power system
children.definition: Those units and components which furnish hydraulic fluid under pressure (includes pumps, regulators, lines, valves, etc.) to a common point (manifold) for redistribution to other defined systems.

children.name: 2910 Hydraulic system - Main
children.definition: That portion of the system which is used to store and deliver hydraulic fluid to using systems. Includes items such as tanks, accumulators, valves,  pumps, levers, switches, cables, plumbing, wiring, external connectors, etc. Does not include the supply valves to the using systems.

children.name: 2920 Hydraulic system - Auxiliary
children.definition: That portion of the system which is classified as auxiliary, emergency or standby, and which is used to supplement or take the place of the main hydraulic system. Includes items such as tanks and accumulators which are separate from the main system, hand pumps, auxiliary pumps, valves, plumbing, wiring, etc.

children.name: 2930 Hydraulic indicating system
children.definition: That portion of the system which is used to indicate the quantity, temperature and pressure of the hydraulic fluid. Includes items such as transmitters, indicators, wiring, warning systems, etc.

children.name: Hydraulic fluid temperature
children.definition: The hydraulic fluid temperature is outside of the normal operating range

children.name: Hydraulic - Total system loss
children.definition: A total loss of fluid from a hydraulic system

children.name: Hydraulic low reservoir pressure
children.definition: A reduction in reservoir pressure which may or may not result in a warning

children.name: Hydraulic leak (Visible)
children.definition: A visible leak of hydraulic fluid either pre-departure or during flight

children.name: Hydraulic low pressure
children.definition: The supplied hydraulic pressure is lower than the normal system operating pressure

children.name: Hydraulic main pump
children.definition: A fault or defect with a main hydraulic pump

children.name: Hydraulic standby pump
children.definition: A fault or defect with a standby hydraulic pump

children.name: Hydraulic electric pump
children.definition: A fault or defect with an electric hydraulic pump

children.name: Hydraulic - System loss
children.definition: A significant reduction in a hydraulic system fluid quantity

children.name: Hydraulic quantity
children.definition: The hydraulic quantity is outside of the normal operating range. Can be either too high or too low

children.name: Hydraulic noise
children.definition: Unexpected noise/vibration from Hydraulic system

children.name: 3000 Ice/Rain protection system
children.definition: Safety report related to the Tice/rain protection system which provide a means of preventing or disposing of formation of ice and rain on various parts of the aircraft. Includes alcohol pump, valves, tanks, propeller/rotor anti-icing system, wing heaters, water line heaters, pitot heaters, scoop heaters, windshield wipers and the electrical and heated air portion of windshield ice control. Does not include the basic windshield panel. For turbine type power plants using air as the anti-icing medium, engine anti-icing is contained under Air System.

children.name: 3010 Airfoil anti/de-ice system
children.definition: Safety report related to the airfoil anti/de-ice system which is used to eliminate or prevent the formation of ice on all airfoil surfaces. Includes wings, airfoil sections of the empennage, and pylons.

children.name: 3020 Air intake anti/de-ice system
children.definition: Safety report related to the air intake/de-ice system which is used to eliminate or prevent the formation of ice in or around air intakes. Includes power plant cowling anti-icing.

children.name: 3030 Pitot/Static anti-ice system
children.definition: Safety report related to the pitot/static anti-ice system which is used to eliminate or prevent the formation of ice on the pitot and static systems.

children.name: 3040 Windshield/door rain/ice removal
children.definition: Safety report related to the windshield/door rain/ice removal system which is used to eliminate or prevent the formation of ice, frost or rain on the Windows, windshields and doors.

children.name: 3050 Antenna/Radome anti-ice/de-ice system
children.definition: Safety report related to the antenna/radome anti-ice/de-ice system which is used to eliminate or prevent the formation of ice on antennas and radomes.

children.name: 3060 Prop/Rotor anti-ice/de-ice system
children.definition: Safety report related to the prop/rotor anti-ice/de-ice system which is used to eliminate or prevent the formation of ice on propellers or rotors. Includes all components up to but not including rotating assembly.

children.name: 3070 Water line anti-ice system
children.definition: Safety report related to the water line anti-ice system which is used to prevent the formation of ice in water supply and drain lines.

children.name: 3080 Ice detection
children.definition: Safety report related to the ice detection system which is used to detect and indicate the formation of ice.

children.name: 3097 Ice/Rain protection system wiring
children.definition: Safety report related to the ice/rain protectin system wiring discrepancies

children.name: Engine anti-icing
children.definition: A fault with/or failure of the engine anti-icing system

children.name: Airframe anti-icing
children.definition: A fault with/or failure of the airframe anti-icing system

children.name: Windscreen heating
children.definition: A fault with/or failure of the windscreen heating system

children.name: Windscreen wipers
children.definition: A fault with the windscreen wipers which results in their poor performance

children.name: Rain repellent
children.definition: A leak of the repellent within the flightdeck or onto a flight deck window, or event involving rain repellent

children.name: Engine de-icing
children.definition: A fault with/or failure of the engine de-icing system

children.name: Airframe de-icing
children.definition: A fault with/or failure of the airframe de-icing system

children.name: 3100 Indicating/Recording system
children.definition: Safety report related to the Pictorial coverage of all instruments, instrument panels and controls. Procedural coverage of those systems which give visual or aural warning of conditions in unrelated systems. Units which record, store or compute data from unrelated systems. Includes systems/units which integrate indicating instruments into a central display system and instruments not related to any specific system.

children.name: 3110 Instrument panel
children.definition: Safety report related to the Coverage of all panels fixed or movable with their replaceable components such as instruments, switches, circuit breakers, fuses, etc. Also includes general coverage of instrument panel vibrators and other panel accessories.

children.name: 3120 Independent instruments (clock, etc.)
children.definition: Safety report related to the instruments, units and components which are not related to specific systems. Includes items such as inclinometers, clocks, etc.

children.name: 3130 Data recorders (FLT/maint)
children.definition: Safety report related to the systems and components used for recording data not related to specific systems. Includes items such as flight recorders, performance or maintenance recorders, VG recorders, etc.

children.name: 3140 Central computers (EICAS)
children.definition: Safety report related to the systems and components used for computing data from a number of different sources without a preponderance of functions in any one system. Includes items such as Digital Core Avionic System (DCAS), stored check list, emergency procedures, company regulations, etc., for call up on a display, integrated instrument systems such as engine, airplane power and central warning indicators when combined into a central display.

children.name: 3150 Central warning
children.definition: Safety report related to the central warning systems and components which give audible or visual warning of conditions in unrelated systems. Includes items such as master warning or flight warning systems, central instrument warning, or caution and warning systems, tone generators, annunciators, etc.

children.name: 3160 Central display
children.definition: Safety report related to the central display systems and components which give visual display of conditions in unrelated systems.

children.name: 3170 Automatic data
children.definition: Safety report related to the  systems and components used for collating and computing data from unrelated systems and transmitting same automatically. Includes ASDAR systems and components.

children.name: Machmeter
children.definition: A fault or failure of a machmeter

children.name: Standby instruments
children.definition: A fault or failure of any standby instrument

children.name: Clock
children.definition: A fault or failure of the aircraft clock

children.name: Airspeed indicator
children.definition: A fault or failure of an airspeed indicator

children.name: Altimeter
children.definition: A fault or failure of an altimeter

children.name: ADI/PFD
children.definition: A fault or failure of the attitude director indicator/primary flight display

children.name: HSI/ND
children.definition: A fault or failure of a horizontal situation indicator

children.name: VSI
children.definition: A fault or failure of the vertical speed indicator/navigation display

children.name: EICAS/ECAM
children.definition: A fault or failure which is connected to the Engine Indication (and) Crew-Alerting System or Electrical Flight Indicating System

children.name: Instrument panel
children.definition: Includes security of the panel but not panel lighting

children.name: Pitot probe
children.definition: An abnormal instrument indication which can be attributed to a defective pitot probe.

children.name: Central warning system
children.definition: A failure in the central warning system

children.name: Multiple instrument failures
children.definition: Normally as a result of a significant electrical failures

children.name: Static vents
children.definition: An abnormal instrument indication which can be attributed to a defective static vent

children.name: 3200 Landing gear system
children.definition: Safety report related to the landing gear sytem units and components which furnish a means of supporting and steering the aircraft on the Groundor water, and make it possible to retract and store the landing gear in flight. Includes tail skid assembly, brakes, wheels, floats, skids, skis, doors, shock struts, tires, linkages, position indicating and warning systems. Also includes the functioning and maintenance aspects of the landing gear doors but does not include the structure.

children.name: 3210 Main landing gear
children.definition: Safety report related to the main landing gear system which provides the major support for the aircraft while on the ground. Includes items such as shock struts, bogie axles, drag struts, doors, linkages, attach bolts, etc.

children.name: 3220 Nose/Tail landing gear
children.definition: Safety report related to the nose/tail landing gear system which supports the nose of the aircraft while the aircraft is on the ground. Includes items such as shock struts, drag struts, doors, linkages, attach bolts, etc.

children.name: 3230 Landing gear retract/extend system
children.definition: Safety report related to the landing gear retract/extend system which is used to extend and retract the landing gear and open and close the landing gear doors. Includes items such as actuating mechanisms, bogie trim, bungees, up and down latches, operating controls, valves and motors, cables, wiring, plumbing, etc.

children.name: 3240 Landing gear brake system
children.definition: Safety report related to the landing gear brake system which provides for rolling and stopping the aircraft while on the Ground and stopping wheel rotation after retraction. Includes items such as bearings, tires, valves, de-boosters, swivel glands, anti-skid devices, pressure indicators, plumbing, etc.

children.name: 3250 Landing gear steering system
children.definition: Safety report related to the landing gear steering system which is used to control the direction of movement of the aircraft on the ground. Includes items such as actuating cylinders, controls, bogie swivel unlock, etc.

children.name: 3260 Landing gear position and warning
children.definition: Safety report related to the landing gear position and warning system which is used to indicate and warn of the position of the landing gear/doors. Includes items such as switches, relays, lights, indicators, horns, wiring, etc.

children.name: 3270 Auxiliary gear (tail skid)
children.definition: Safety report related to the devices used to stabilize the aircraft while on the Ground and prevent damage by Ground contact. Includes items such as shock strut, skid block, wheels, etc.

children.name: Anti-skid
children.definition: A fault or failure within the anti skid system which results in a degradation of braking efficiency

children.name: Autobrake
children.definition: A defect within the autobrake system which results in manual braking only being available

children.name: Body gear steering
children.definition: The body gear steering fails to operate or return to the neutral position

children.name: Brakes
children.definition: A defect or failure of an individual or of several wheel brakes

children.name: Gear failed to extend
children.definition: The landing gear has failed to move from the locked up position

children.name: Gear failed to retract
children.definition: The landing gear has failed to move from the locked down position

children.name: Gear failed to lock down/up
children.definition: A flight deck indication that the landing gear is neither locked up or down

children.name: Gear doors not secured
children.definition: The landing gear doors do not indicate locked up or down

children.name: Nosewheel steering
children.definition: A defect with the nosewheel steering which results in a reduction of manoeuvrability while on the ground

children.name: Brake overheat
children.definition: A flight deck indication that a brake overheat condition exists

children.name: Tyres/Wheels
children.definition: A failure of a tyre or wheel

children.name: Gear - Vibration/Shimmy
children.definition: Significant landing gear vibration or nosewheel shimmy is experienced

children.name: Gear collapsed
children.definition: A partial or total collapse of one or more landing gear legs

children.name: Landing gear lever
children.definition: An incident due to a fault with the landing gear lever

children.name: Tyre deflated
children.definition: Flight Deck indicated or noticed during pre or post flight inspection

children.name: Parking brake
children.definition: A defect with the parking brake or when the parking brake has failed to prevent the aircraft from moving

children.name: Gear - False indication
children.definition: False indication of landing gear position

children.name: Tyre pressure indication system
children.definition: A TPIS (Tyre Pressure Indication System) alert received during taxy or inflight

children.name: Gear slow to retract/extend
children.definition: Excessive time elapsed during retraction or extension of the landing gear

children.name: 3300 Lighting system
children.definition: Safety report related to the lighting system units and components (electrically powered) which provide for external and internal illumination such as landing lights, taxi lights, position lights, rotating lights, ice lights, master warning lights, passenger reading and cabin dome lights, etc. Includes light fixtures, switches and wiring. Does not include warning lights for individual systems or self-illuminating signs.

children.name: 3310 Flight compartment lighting
children.definition: Safety report related to the lighting sub-systems in the compartment above the floor and between the forward passenger partition and the forward pressure dome. Does not include cargo compartment. Includes direct and indirect illumination of work areas, panels, and instruments. Includes master warning light and warning light dimming systems, where not integrated with a central audio or visual system under 31-50.

children.name: 3320 Passenger compartment lighting
children.definition: Safety report related to the lighting sub-systems in the areas in which the passengers are seated and in buffet/galley, lavatories, lounges and coat rooms. Includes items such as direct and indirect illumination, passenger call system, lighted signs, etc.

children.name: 3330 Cargo compartment lighting
children.definition: Safety report related to the lighting sub-systems in the compartments for stowage of cargo and the housing of various components of accessories

children.name: 3340 Exterior lighting
children.definition: Safety report related to the lighting sub-systems used to provide illumination outside of the aircraft. Includes lights such as landing, navigation, position indicating, wing illumination, rotating, courtesy, taxi, etc.

children.name: 3350 emergency lighting
children.definition: Safety report related to the separate and independent subsystem used to provide illumination in case of primary electrical power failure. Includes items such as inertia flashlights, lanterns, etc.

children.name: Landing/Taxi lights
children.definition: A filament failure which affects aircraft navigation while taxiing at night

children.name: Anti-collision light
children.definition: A filament failure resulting in reduced aircraft visibility

children.name: Flight deck/instrument lighting
children.definition: Deficiencies with instrument lighting or lighting in the flight deck which affects the safe operation of the flight

children.name: Cabin lighting
children.definition: A defect or failure of normal cabin lighting

children.name: Emergency lights
children.definition: A defect or failure with the emergency lighting system

children.name: Navigation/Strobe lights
children.definition: A failure of, or damage to the navigation or strobe lights

children.name: Passenger signs
children.definition: A significant failure of a cabin sign which degrades passenger safety

children.name: 3400 Navigation system
children.definition: Safety report related to the navigation system units and components which provide aircraft navigational information. Includes VOR, pitot, static, ILS, flight director, compasses, indicators, etc.

children.name: 3410 Flight environment data
children.definition: Safety report related to the flight environment data system which senses environmental conditions and uses the data to influence navigation. Includes such items as Central Air Data Computers, pitot/static systems, air temperature, rate-of-climb, airspeed, high speed warning, altitude, altitude reporting, altimeter correction system, air disturbance detection system, etc.

children.name: 3420 Attitude and direction data system
children.definition: Safety report related to the attitude and direction data system which uses magnetic or inertia forces to sense and display the direction or attitude of the aircraft. This includes sensing, computing, indicating and warning devices such as magnetic compasses, vertical and directional references, magnetic heading systems, attitude director systems, symbol generators, turn and bank, rate of turn, amplifiers, indicators, etc. Includes Flight Director when it is not integral with the auto pilot computation.

children.name: 3430 Landing and taxi aids
children.definition: Safety report related to the landing and taxi aids system which provides guidance during approach, landing and taxiing. Includes items such as localizer, glide slope, ILS, markers, paravisual director Ground guidance systems, etc.

children.name: 3440 Independent pos. determining system
children.definition: Safety report related to the independent pos. determining system which provides information to determine position and is mainly independent of Ground installations or orbital satellites. Includes items such as inertial guidance systems, weather radar, doppler, proximity warning, collision avoidance, star tracker, etc. Also includes sextants/octants, etc.

children.name: 3450 Dependent position determining
children.definition: Safety report related to the dependent position determining system which provides information to determine position and is mainly dependent on Ground installations or orbital satellites. Includes items such as DME, transponders, radio compass, LORAN, VOR, ADF, OMEGA, GLOBAL POSITIONING, etc.

children.name: 3460 Flight manage. computing hardware
children.definition: Safety report related to the flight mamage. computing hardware system which combines navigational data to compute or manage the aircraft s geographical position or theoretical flight path. Includes items such as course computers, flight management computers, performance data computers, and associated control display units, warning annunciators, etc.

children.name: ADF
children.definition: A failure of both or a significant discrepancy between the two automatic direction finder units

children.name: GPS
children.definition: A total or partial failure of the Global Positioning System

children.name: VOR
children.definition: A single or double failure of the VHF Omni-Directional Radio Range units or a significant discrepancy between the two

children.name: FMS/FMC
children.definition: A single or double failure of an Flight Management System or Computer

children.name: CDU/MCDU
children.definition: A single or double failure of a control display unit

children.name: INS/IRS
children.definition: A failure of one or more Inertial Navigation Unit or Inertial Navigation Systems

children.name: Radio altimeter
children.definition: Failure of a radio altimeter

children.name: Weather radar
children.definition: A single or double weather radar failure

children.name: ILS/MLS
children.definition: A failure of the Microwave Landing System

children.name: DME
children.definition: A total failure of the distance measuring equipment

children.name: Transponder
children.definition: A total failure of the ATC transponder

children.name: Double failure
children.definition: Normally used for double failures in one system

children.name: TCAS failure
children.definition: A failure within the Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System system

children.name: EGPWS/GPWS failure
children.definition: An associated defect which requires the (Enhanced) Ground Proximity Warning System to be selected OFF, or a total system failure

children.name: Map shift
children.definition: A discrepancy that exists between the aircraft indicated and actual position

children.name: ADC
children.definition: A defect with/or failure of an ADC/DADC/CADC during flight

children.name: 3500 Oxygen system
children.definition: Safety report related to the oxygen system which stores, regulate, and deliver oxygen to the passengers and crew, including bottles, relief valves, shut-off valves, outlets, regulators, masks, walkaround bottles, etc.

children.name: 3510 Crew oxygen system
children.definition: Safety report related to the crew oxygen system which furnishes oxygen to the crew.

children.name: 3520 Passenger oxygen system
children.definition: Safety report related to the pasenger oxygen system which furnishes oxygen to the passengers.

children.name: 3530 Portable oxygen system
children.definition: Safety report related to the portable oxygen system which has an independent oxygen supply and which can be transported about the airplane.

children.name: Passenger oxygen
children.definition: A defect with, or failure of passenger oxygen

children.name: Crew oxygen
children.definition: A defect with, or failure of crew oxygen

children.name: Portable oxygen
children.definition: A defect with or failure of portable oxygen

children.name: Crew mask
children.definition: A defect with a crew mask which renders it unusable

children.name: Passenger mask
children.definition: A defect with a passenger oxygen mask which renders it unusable

children.name: Oxygen - Leak
children.definition: A significant leak in either the crew or passenger oxygen system

children.name: Oxygen - Low quantity
children.definition: Low oxygen quantity, not as a result of a leak

children.name: 3600 Pneumatic system
children.definition: Safety report related to the pneumatic system units and components (Ducts and Valves) which deliver large volumes of compressed air from a power source to connecting points for such other systems as air conditioning, pressurization, deicing, etc.

children.name: 3610 Pneumatic distribution system
children.definition: Safety report related to the pneumatic distribution system which is used to distribute high or low-pressure air to using systems. Includes items such as ducts, valves, actuators, heat exchangers, controls, etc. Does not include the supply valves to the using systems.

children.name: 3620 Pneumatic indicating system
children.definition: Safety report related to the pneumatic indicating system which is used to indicate temperature and pressure of the pneumatic system. Includes temperature and pressure warning systems.

children.name: Duct - Leak
children.definition: A duct leak has occurred normally accompanied by a flight deck warning

children.name: Duct - Contaminated
children.definition: An air conditioning system has been affected by a contaminated pneumatic duct

children.name: Duct - Overheat
children.definition: A duct overheat has occurred normally accompanied by a flight deck warning

children.name: Duct - Failure
children.definition: A duct failure has occurred normally accompanied by a flight deck warning

children.name: Strut overheat
children.definition: A strut overheat which results in a flight deck warning

children.name: Valve failure
children.definition: A failure of any other valve in the pneumatic system except the bleed valve

children.name: Bleed valve
children.definition: A defect with the bleed valve or the inability to control it from the flight deck

children.name: Wing/Body overheat
children.definition: An flight deck indication of a wing or body overheat

children.name: 3700 Vacuum system
children.definition: Safety report related to the vaccum system units and components used to generate, deliver and regulate negative air pressure, including pumps, regulators, lines, etc., through and including the manifold.

children.name: 3710 Vacuum distribution system
children.definition: Safety report related to the vaccum distribution system which is used to distribute negative pressure air to using systems.

children.name: 3720 Vacuum indicating system
children.definition: Safety report related to that portion of the system which is used to indicate pressure. Includes pressure warning system.

children.name: 4400 Cabin system
children.definition: Safety report related to the cabin system which furnish a means of entertaining the passengers and providing communication within the aircraft and between the aircraft cabin and Ground stations. Includes voice, data, music and video transmissions. Does not include SATCOM, HF, VHF, UHF and all transmitting/receiving equipment, antennas, etc.

children.name: 4410 Cabin core system
children.definition: Safety report related to the cabin core system used to accomplish the integrated functional control, operation, testing and monitoring of cabin systems and to increase cabin comfort (such as active noise control). Includes items such as controllers, cabin control panels, handsets, signs, loudspeakers, etc.

children.name: 4420 In-flight entertainment system
children.definition: Safety report related to the in-flight entertainment system used to entertain the passengers with music, video, information, games, etc. Includes items such as controllers, cabin control panels, audio and video equipment, etc.

children.name: 4430 External communication system
children.definition: Safety report related to the external communication system used by System passengers and cabin crew to transmit and/or receive data/messages from air to air or from air to Ground installations. Includes items such as telephones, telefaxes, modems, AM/FM radio units, etc.

children.name: 4440 Cabin mass memory system
children.definition: Safety report related to the cabin mass memory system used to store and process cabin related data, such as systems configuration data, multimedia programs, etc. Includes items such as controllers, terminals, keyboards, disk drives, printers, modems, etc.

children.name: 4450 Cabin monitoring system
children.definition: Safety report related to the cabin monitoring system used to monitor parts of the cabin area. Includes items such as surveillance cameras, monitors, etc. Does not include external anti-hijack devices or external video monitoring.

children.name: 4460 Miscellaneous cabin system
children.definition: Safety report related to the miscellaneous cabin system used to support miscellaneous cabin functions.

children.name: 4500 On-board maintenance system
children.definition: Safety report related to the onboard maintenance units, components and associated system which interfaces with multiple aircraft systems. Contains checkout and fault isolation procedures using a central computer complex and/or standard fault isolation procedures to locate a single system or component malfunction.

children.name: 4510 Central maintenance system
children.definition: Safety report related to the central maintenance system

children.name: 4520 Up and down data loading system
children.definition: Safety report related to the up and down data loading system

children.name: 4540 Printer
children.definition: Safety report related to the printer

children.name: 4550 Structure monitoring
children.definition: Safety report related to the Central Maintenance System interfaces with Structures, and identification of maintenance functions related to Structures.

children.name: 4600 Information systems
children.definition: Safety report related to the information systems units and components which furnish a means of storing, updating, and retrieving digital information traditionally provided on paper, microfilm, or microfiche. Includes units that are dedicated to the information storage and retrieval function such as the Electronic Library mass storage and controller. Does not include units or components installed for other uses and shared with other systems, such as flight deck printer or general use display.

children.name: 4610 Airplane general information systems
children.definition: Safety report related to the airplane general information systems

children.name: 4620 Flight deck information systems
children.definition: Safety report related to the the onboard information system that supports the flight deck systems, flight deck crew and flight operations

children.name: 4630 Maintenance information systems
children.definition: Safety report related to the onboard flight information system that supports all onboard maintenance system functions, maintenance technicians, and any Ground based maintenance activity.

children.name: 4640 Passenger cabin information systems
children.definition: Safety report related to the onboard information system that supports the passenger cabin, cabin operations, and flight attendants.

children.name: 4650 Miscellaneous information systems
children.definition: That portion of the onboard information system that supports other functions as defined by the user that cannot be related to the flight deck, passenger cabin, or maintenance.

children.name: 4700 Inert gas system
children.definition: Safety report related to the inert gas system units and components used to generate, store, deliver and regulate inert gas. Includes regulators, lines, manifolds, etc.

children.name: 4710 Generation/Storage
children.definition: Safety report related to the general/storage system which generates and/or stores inert gas. Includes tanks, cells, reservoirs, accumulators, etc. Does not include plumbing, pumps, valves, controls, etc.

children.name: 4720 Distribution
children.definition: Safety report related to the distribution system which is used to distribute inert gas to the using systems. Includes plumbing, pumps, valves, regulators, etc.

children.name: 4730 Control
children.definition: Safety report related to the inert gas controls which meter the inert gas to the distribution components and into the using systems. Includes items such as levers, switches, cables, etc.

children.name: 4740 Indicating
children.definition: Safety report related to the system which is used to indicate the flow rate, temperature and pressure of the inert gas. Includes items such as transmitters, indicators, etc.

children.name: 5300 Fuselage structure (general)
children.definition: Safety report related to the Structural units and associated components and members which make up the compartments for equipment, passengers, crew, cargo, plus the structure of the envelope and gondola of airships. Includes skins, belt frames, stringers, floor beams, floor, pressure dome, scuppers, tail cone, fuselage-to-wing-andempennage fillets, attach/attached fittings, load curtains, cables, ballonets, etc.

children.name: 5301 Aerial tow equipment
children.definition: Safety report related to the aerial tow equipment

children.name: 5302 Rotorcraft tail boom
children.definition: Safety report related to the rotorcraft tail boom

children.name: 5310 Fuselage main - Structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the fuselage main, structure

children.name: 5320 Fuselage miscellaneous structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the fuselage miscellaneous structure

children.name: 5330 Fuselage main - Plate/Skin
children.definition: Safety report related to the fuselage main plate/skin

children.name: 5340 Fuselage main - Attach fittings
children.definition: Safety report related to the fuselage main, attach fittings

children.name: 5350 Aerodynamic fairings
children.definition: Safety report related to the aerodynamic fairings

children.name: 5400 Nacelle/Pylon structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the Structural units and associated components and members which furnish a means of mounting and housing the power plant or rotor assembly. Includes skins, longerons, belt frames, stringers, clamshells, scuppers, doors, nacelle fillets, attach/attached fittings, etc. Also includes the structure of power plant cowling inclusive of the structural portion of the inlet whether or not integral with the aircraft. Structural portions of the exhaust system are excluded where they are not integral with the airframe.

children.name: 5410 Nacelle/Pylon - Main frame
children.definition: Safety report related to the nacelle/pylon, main frame

children.name: 5420 Nacelle/Pylon miscellaneous
children.definition: Safety report related to the nacelle/pylon miscellaneous

children.name: 5500 Empennage structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the Horizontal and vertical stabilizers including the structure of the elevator and rudder.

children.name: 5510 Horizontal stabilizer structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the horizontal airfoil of the tail or nose section to which the elevator is attached. Includes items such as spars, ribs, stringers, skins, access covers, tips, attach/attached fittings, etc.

children.name: 5520 Elevator structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the Removable airfoil which is attached to the horizontal stabilizer or canard and used for pitch control. Includes items such as spars, ribs, stringers, skins, access covers, tabs, balance devices, attach/ attached fittings, etc.

children.name: 5530 Vertical stabilizer structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the Vertical airfoil to which the rudder is attached. Includes items such as spars, ribs, stringers, skins, access covers, tips, attach/attached fittings, etc.

children.name: 5540 Rudder structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the Removable airfoil which is attached to the vertical stabilizer and used for yaw control. Includes items such as spars, ribs, stringers, skins, access covers, tabs, balance devices, attach/attached fittings, etc.

children.name: 5550 Empennage FLT. CONT., attach fitting
children.definition: Safety report related to the empennage, flight controls and attachment fittings

children.name: 5700 Wing structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the Center wing and outer wing structural units and associated components and members which support the aircraft in flight. Includes spars, skin, ribs, stringers, clamshells, scuppers, etc., and integral fuel tank structure of the flaps, slats, ailerons or elevons (complete with tabs), spoilers, and wing folding system.

children.name: 5710 Wing - Main frame structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the Skins, primary structure, fillets, and fairings of the center wing, and attach/attached fittings.

children.name: 5720 Wing miscellaneous structure
children.definition: Safety report related to the Skins, primary structure, fillets, and fairings of the outer wing, and attach/attached fittings.

children.name: 5730 Wing -  Plates/Skins
children.definition: Safety report related to the wing, plates/skins

children.name: 5740 Wing - Attach fittings
children.definition: Safety report related to the wing, attach fittings

children.name: 5750 Wing - Control surfaces
children.definition: Safety report related to the wing, control surfaces

children.name: Propeller - Overspeed
children.definition: When the propeller operates outside of the maximum designed operating speed

children.name: Propeller - Separation
children.definition: A section of propeller departs from the engine

children.name: Propeller - Control
children.definition: A defect within the pitch change mechanism of the propeller

children.name: Propeller - Autofeather system
children.definition: A failure within the propeller auto feathering system

children.name: Propeller - Failed to feather
children.definition: The propeller fails to feather upon selection

children.name: Propeller - Uncommanded feather
children.definition: A propeller that feathers without selection

children.name: Propeller - Oil
children.definition: Any significant leak or loss of propeller oil

children.name: Propeller - Insecure
children.definition: The propeller or a component within the propeller is not correctly secured

children.name: Propeller - Restraint
children.definition: A failure of the propeller restraint causing an unsafe situation

children.name: Propeller - Damage
children.definition: Significant damage to an engine propellor found either pre flight or post flight

children.name: 7100 Powerplant system
children.definition: Safety report related to the powerplant system i.e. the overall power package inclusive of engine, air intake, mount, cowling, scoops, cowl flaps.

children.name: 7110 Engine cowling system
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine cowling system i.e. the removable coverings which extend over and around the power plant assembly. Includes the functioning and maintenance aspects of items such as accessory section cowls, cowl flaps, cowling supports, and attach and locking mechanisms, etc. Does not include the structure integral with the airframe.

children.name: 7120 Engine mount section
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine mount section framework, either of build-up construction or forgings which support the engine and attach it to the nacelle or pylon. Includes items such as engine mounts, vibration dampeners, support links, mounting bolts, etc.

children.name: 7130 Engine fireseals
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine fireseals i.e., the fire-resistant partitions and seals mounted on or about the power package for the purpose of isolating areas subject to fire.

children.name: 7160 Engine air intake system
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine air intake system of the power plant system which directs and may or may not vary the mass air flow to the engine. Includes items such as nose ring cowls, scoops, compressor fan cowls, buried engine ducts, vortex generators, actuators, control handles, cables, wiring, plumbing, linkages, doors, warning systems, position indicators, etc. Does not include integral structure with the airframe.

children.name: 7170 Engine drains
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine drain components and manifold assemblies which are used to drain off excess fluids from the power plant and its accessories. Includes drainlines, manifolds, tanks, flame arrestors, vents, and their supporting brackets, etc. Also includes components that are an integral part of, or fitted to the power plant cowling.

children.name: 7200 Engine (turbine/turboprop)
children.definition: Safety report related to general information, limits and procedures. In the engine overhaul manual this section would include such subjects as tear down, cleaning, inspection, assembly, testing, etc.

children.name: 7210 Turbine engine reduction gear
children.definition: Safety report related to the turbine engine reduction gear section of the engine which contains the propeller shafts and reduction gears. Includes items such as drives for hose mounted accessories, etc. If applicable, the section of the engine which uses mechanical force, through a geardriven system, to drive front mounted propulsors which provide the majority of the energy generated. Includes items such as Propulsor Blades, Actuation Systems, Reduction Gears, Drive-Shafts, etc.

children.name: 7220 Turbine engine air inlet section
children.definition: Safety report related to the turbine engine air inlet section of the engine through which the air enters the compressor section. Includes items such as guide vanes, shrouds, cases, etc.

children.name: 7230 Turbine engine compressor section
children.definition: Safety report related to the turbine engine compressor section of the engine in which the air is compressed. Includes items such as cases, vanes, shrouds, rotors, diffusers, etc. Also includes the maintenance and overhaul of stator blades but not the operation of variable stator blades which is covered under [Chapter (System) 75 - 30]. Does not include compressor bleed system.

children.name: 7240 Turbine engine combustion section
children.definition: Safety report related to the turbine engine combustion section of the engine in which the air and fuel are combined and burned. Includes items such as burner cans, cases, etc.

children.name: 7250 Turbine section
children.definition: Safety report related to the turbine engine section of the engine containing the turbines. Includes items such as turbine nozzles, turbine rotors, cases, etc.

children.name: 7260 Turbine engine accessory drive
children.definition: Safety report related to the mechanical power take-offs to drive accessories. Includes items such as engine-mounted gear boxes, gears, seals, pumps, etc. Does not include remotely installed gear boxes.

children.name: 7270 Turbine engine bypass section
children.definition: Safety report related to the section of the engine which bypasses a portion of the normal engine airflow (either ram or compressed air) for the prime purpose of adding to engine thrust or reducing specific fuel consumption.

children.name: 7300 Engine fuel and control
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine and fuel control for turbine engines, those units and components and associated mechanical systems or electrical circuits which furnish or control fuel to the engine beyond the main fuel quick disconnect; and thrust augmenter, fuel flow rate sensing, transmitting and/or indicating units whether the units are before or beyond the quick disconnect.

children.name: 7310 Engine fuel distribution
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine fuel distribution portion of the system from the main quick disconnect to the engine, which distributes fuel to the engine burner section and the thrust augmenter. Includes items such as plumbing, pumps, temperature regulators, valves, filters, manifold, nozzles, etc. Does not include the main or thrust augmenter fuel control.

children.name: 7320 Fuel controlling system
children.definition: Safety report related to the main fuel controlling system which meters fuel to the engine and to the thrust augmenter. Includes items such as hydromechanical or electronic fuel control, levers, actuators, cables, pulleys, linkages, sensors, valves, etc., which are components of the fuel control units.

children.name: 7330 Engine fuel indicating system
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine fuel indicating system which is used to indicate the flow rate, temperature and pressure of the fuel. Includes items such as transmitters, indicators, wiring, etc. Does not include indication.

children.name: 7400 Ignition system
children.definition: Safety report related to the ignition system units and components which generate, control, furnish, or distribute an electrical current to ignite the fuel air mixture in the cylinders of reciprocating engines or in the combustion chambers or thrust augmenters of turbine engines. Includes induction vibrators, magnetos, switches, lead filters, distributors, harnesses, plugs, ignition relays, exciters, and the electrical portion of spark advance.

children.name: 7410 Ignition power supply
children.definition: Safety report related to the ignition power supply portion of the system which generates electrical current for the purpose of igniting the fuel mixture in the combustion chambers and thrust augmenters. Includes items such as magnetos, distributors, booster coils, exciters, transformers, storage capacitors and compositors, etc.

children.name: 7420 Ignition harness (distribution)
children.definition: Safety report related to the ignition harness (distribution) portion of the system which conducts high or low voltage electricity from the electrical power supply to the spark plugs, or igniters. Includes wiring between magneto and distributor in those systems where they are separate units. Includes items such as ignition harness, high tension leads, coils as used in "low tension" systems, spark plugs, igniters, etc.

children.name: 7430 Ignition/Starter switching
children.definition: Safety report related to the ignition/starter switching portion of the system which provides a means of rendering the electrical power supply inoperative. Includes items such as ignition switches, wiring, connectors, etc.

children.name: 7500 Engine bleed air system
children.definition: For turbine engines, those external units and components and integral basic engine parts which go together to conduct air to various portions of the engine and to the extension shaft and torquemeter, assembly, if any.Includes compressor bleed systems  used to control flow of air through the  engine, cooling air systems and heated air systems for engine anti-icing. Does not include aircraft anti-icing, engine starting systems, nor exhaust supplementary air systems.

children.name: 7510 Engine anti-icing system
children.definition: That portion of the system which is used to eliminate and prevent the formation of ice by bleed air in all parts of the engine, excluding power plant cowling which is covered under [Chapter (System) 30]. Includes items such as valves, plumbing, wiring,  regulators, etc.

children.name: 7520 Engine cooling system
children.definition: That portion of the system which is used to ventilate the engine and accessories. Includes items such as valves, plumbing, wiring, jet pumps, vortex spoilers, etc.

children.name: 7530 Compressor bleed control
children.definition: That portion of the system which is used to control the flow of air through the engine. Includes items such as governors, valves, actuators, linkages, etc. Also includes the operation of variable stator blades, but not the maintenance and overhaul.

children.name: 7540 Bleed air indicating system
children.definition: That portion of the system which is used to indicate temperature, pressure, control positions, etc., of the air systems. Includes items such as transmitters, indicators, wiring, etc.

children.name: 7600 Engine controls
children.definition: Safety report related to those controls which govern operation of the engine. Includes units and components which are interconnected for emergency shutdown. For turbo-prop engines, includes linkages and controls to the coordinator or equivalent to the propeller governor, fuel control unit or other units being controlled. For reciprocating engines, includes controls for blowers. Does not include units or components which are specifically included in other chapters.

children.name: 7601 Engine synchronizing
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine synchronizing controls which govern operation of the engine.

children.name: 7602 Mixture control
children.definition: Safety report related to the mixture controls which govern operation of the engine.

children.name: 7603 Power lever
children.definition: Safety report related to thepower lever controls which govern operation of the engine.

children.name: 7620 Engine emergency shutdown system
children.definition: Safety report related to that portion of the system which furnishes a means of controlling the flow of fluids to and from the engine during emergency procedures. Includes items such as levers, cables, pulleys, linkages, switches, wiring, etc. Does not include the units themselves.

children.name: 7700 Engine indicating system
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine indicating system, units, components and associated systems which indicate engine operation. Includes indicators, transmitters, analyzers, etc. For turboprop engines includes phase detectors. Does not include systems or items which are specifically included in other chapters except when indication is accomplished as part of an integrated engine instrument system

children.name: 7710 Power indicating system
children.definition: Safety report related to the power indicating system which directly or indirectly indicates power or thrust. Includes items such as BMEP, pressure-ratio, RPM, etc.

children.name: 7720 Engine temp. indicating system
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine temp.indicating system which indicates temperatures in the engine. Includes items such as cylinder head, exhaust (turbine inlet), etc.

children.name: 7730 Engine ignition analyzer system
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine ignition analyzer system which is used to analyze engine performance or condition by means of instruments or devices such as oscilloscopes, etc. Includes items such as generators, wiring, amplifiers, oscilloscopes, etc.

children.name: 7740 Engine integrated instrument system
children.definition: Safety report related to the portion of the system which is an integrated concept receives several/all engine operating parameters and transmits this to a central processor for crew presentation. Includes items such as display units, transmitters, receivers, computers, etc.

children.name: 7800 Engine exhaust system
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine exhaust system units and components which direct the engine exhaust gases overboard. For turbine engines, includes units external to the basic engine such as thrust reverser and noise suppressor. For reciprocating engines, includes augmenters, stacks, clamps, etc. excludes exhaust-driven turbines.

children.name: 7810 Engine collector/tailpipe/nozzle
children.definition: Safety report related to that portion of the system which collects the exhaust gases from the cylinders or turbines and conducts them overboard. Includes items such as collector rings, exhaust and thrust augmenter ducts, variable nozzles, actuators, plumbing, linkages, wiring, position indicators, warning systems, etc. Does not include power recovery turbines, turbo-superchargers, etc., not noise suppressors or thrust reversers where they are not an integral part of the nozzle system.

children.name: 7820 Engine noise suppressor
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine noise supressor portion of the system which reduces the noise generated by the exhaust gases. Includes items such as pipes, baffles, shields, actuators, plumbing linkages, wiring, position indicators, warning systems, etc. Use - 10 where integral part of nozzle system.

children.name: 7830 Thrust reverser
children.definition: Safety report related to the thrust reverser portion of the system which is used to change the direction of the exhaust gases for reverse thrust. Includes items such as clamshells, linkages, levers, actuators, plumbing, wiring, indicators, warning systems, etc. Use -10 where integral part of nozzle system.

children.name: 7900 Engine oil system (airframe)
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine oil system (airframe) units and components external to the engine concerned with storing and delivering lubricating oil to and from the engine. Covers all units and components from the lubricating oil engine outlet to the inlet, including the inlet and outlet fittings, tank, radiator,by-pass valve, etc., and auxiliary oil systems.

children.name: 7910 Engine oil storage (airframe)
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine oil storage (airframe) portion of the system used for storage of oil. Includes items such as tanks, filling systems, internal hoppers, baffles, tank sump and drain, etc. Does not include tanks which are an integral portion of the engine.

children.name: 7920 Engine oil distribution (airframe)
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine oil distribution (airframe) portion of the system which is used to conduct oil from and to the engine. Includes items such as plumbing, valves, temperature regulator, control systems, etc.

children.name: 7930 Engine oil indicating system
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine oil indicating portion of the system which is used to indicate the quantity, temperature and pressure of the oil. Includes items such as transmitters, indicators, wiring, warning systems, etc. Does not include indication if indication is accomplished as part of an integrated engine instrument system

children.name: 8000 Engine starting system
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine starting system units, components and associated systems used for starting the engine. Includes electrical, inertia air or other starter systems. Does not include ignition systems.

children.name: 8010 Engine cranking
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine cranking portion of the system which is used to perform the cranking portion of the starting operation. Includes items such as plumbing, valves, wiring, starters, switches, relays, etc.

children.name: 8011 Engine starter
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine starter system

children.name: 8097 Engine starting system wiring
children.definition: Safety report related to the engine starting system wiring

children.name: 8120 Exhaust turbocharger
children.definition: Safety report related to the turbines which extract energy from the exhaust gases and are coupled to the crankshaft.

children.name: 8200 Water injection system
children.definition: Safety report related to the water injection system units and components which furnish, meter and inject water or water mixtures into the induction system, includes tanks, pumps, regulators, etc.

children.name: 8300 Accessory gearboxes
children.definition: Safety report related to the accessory gearboxes units and components which are remotely installed and connected to the engine by a drive shaft and hich drive multiple types of accessories. Does not include those accessory drives which are bolted to and are immediately adjacent to the engine.

children.name: High oil consumption
children.definition: The engine oil consumption is considered excessive

children.name: Intake doors/ramps
children.definition: Includes incorrect positioning or sequencing of the intake doors or ramps

children.name: Limit exceedence
children.definition: The engine has been operated outside of the published criteria

children.name: Oil pressure
children.definition: Can include either high, low or fluctuating oil pressure

children.name: Oil quantity
children.definition: Oil quantity reduces below the minimum for normal engine operation or the oil level increases outside the normal operating range

children.name: Oil leak
children.definition: Normally used for leaks found during the pre-departure inspection

children.name: Placard incorrect
children.definition: Normally used for errors in placarding of engine ratings

children.name: Surge/Stall
children.definition: Includes any surge or stall that automatically recovers

children.name: Thrust reverser unlock/unstow
children.definition: The thrust reverser fails to deploy or stow on selection. Or unlocks without selection

children.name: Uncontained failure
children.definition: Debris from the failed engine causes damage to other aircraft parts

children.name: Vibration
children.definition: High engine vibration is indicated or felt

children.name: Throttle stagger
children.definition: Through all stages of engine operation

children.name: Thrust lever/throttle jam/stiff
children.definition: Through all stages of engine operation

children.name: Fluctuating power
children.definition: The engine has failed to achieve the calculated take-off power for the current ambient conditions

children.name: Indication
children.definition: A significant engine indication failure or false engine warning  (not fire warning)

children.name: Hot start
children.definition: An event where an engine start has been aborted due to rapidly rising EGT/TGT

children.name: Low thrust/power
children.definition: Normally used during the take-off phase but can be used through all stages of engine operation

children.name: Damage
children.definition: Would normally be identified during the pre-departure check

children.name: Asymmetric power
children.definition: Through all stages of engine operation

children.name: Fuel leak
children.definition: Normally used for fuel leaks observed during the pre-departure inspection

children.name: Start/Ignition
children.definition: Engine failed to complete starting sequence

children.name: EEC/FADEC
children.definition: Failure of the Engine Electronic Control (or equivalent) system

children.name: Uncommanded power  change
children.definition: Uncommanded variation in power from engine

children.name: Oil contamination
children.definition: Warning of engine oil contamination  e.g. filter by-pass, chip detector, or other contaminants entered oil system (fuel, etc)

children.name: In-flight shutdown
children.definition: An in-flight engine shut down

children.name: Ground shutdown
children.definition: A ground engine shut down

children.name: Rundown
children.definition: Uncommanded engine rundown due to technical defect(s)

children.name: Failed to Shutdown
children.definition: An engine that fails to shutdown during a normal or emergency shutdown procedure

children.name: 3800 Water and waste system
children.definition: Safety report related to the water and waste system fixed units and components which store and deliver for use, fresh water, and those fixed components which store and furnish a means of removal of water and waste. Includes wash basins, toilet assemblies, tanks, valves, etc.

children.name: 3810 Potable water system
children.definition: Safety report related to the potable water system which is used to store and deliver fresh drinking water. Includes wash water system if the potable water is also used for washing.

children.name: 3820 Wash water system
children.definition: Safety report related to the wash water portion of the system which is used to store and deliver wash water which is not potable.

children.name: 3830 Waste disposal system
children.definition: Safety report related to the water disposal portion of the system which is used for disposal of water and waste. Includes items such as wash basins, water closets, flushing systems, etc.

children.name: 3840 Air supply (water press. system)
children.definition: Safety report related to the air supply portion of the system common to more than one sub-system which is used for pressurizing supply tanks to insure fluid flow.

children.name: Evidence of blue ice
children.definition: Evidence of blue ice found during a post flight inspection

children.name: Blue ice shed from aircraft
children.definition: A Ground report has been received regarding blue ice being shed from an aircraft

children.name: Potable water contaminated
children.definition: Contamination of potable drinking water is suspected or confirmed

children.name: Toilet/Lavatory fluid leak in cabin
children.definition: Any fluid leaking from a toilet area

children.name: Potable water leak
children.definition: A water leak whether internal or external from the aircrafts potable water supply

children.name: Toilet/Lavatory full/inoperative
children.definition: A toilet has been reported inoperative or is full rendering it unusable

children.name: 5600 Window/Windshield system
children.definition: Safety report related to the  Fuselage and crew compartment windows inclusive of windshield; also, those windows installed in doors

children.name: 5610 Flight compartment windows
children.definition: Safety report related to the flight compartment windows, i.e., Compartment above the floor and between the forward passenger partition and the forward pressure dome. Includes items such as the transparent material and its frame of sliding and fixed windows and windshields, handles, latching mechanisms, etc. Does not include door or inspection/observation windows.

children.name: 5620 Passenger compartment windows
children.definition: Safety report related to the passenger compartment windows i.e., Area in which the passengers are seated. Includes lounges, lavatories, buffets/galleys and coatrooms. Includes items such as transparent material, its frame, frost shield, etc.

children.name: 5630 Door windows
children.definition: Safety report related to the Door windows used for entrance and exit of the passengers, flight crew and service personnel to and from the airplane. Includes items such as transparent material, its frame, etc. Does not include emergency exit windows.

children.name: 5640 Inspection windows
children.definition: Safety report related to the Windows used for examining compartments and equipment in and about the airplane, and astrodomes used for celestial navigation. Includes items such as transparent material, its frame, etc.

children.name: Overheat - System
children.definition: An event involving a system warning of overheat

children.name: Overheat - False warning
children.definition: False overheat warning

children.name: Loose object
children.definition: Loose object

children.name: Unknown noise/rattle
children.definition: Noise/rattle

children.name: Vibration
children.definition: Vibration/buffet

children.name: AD compliance
children.definition: An event related to AD compliance

children.name: New miss AD breach
children.definition: An event related to a near miss AD breach

children.name: Unapproved data
children.definition: An event related to use of unapproved data

children.name: Defect beyond limits
children.definition: An event involving release of an aircraft with or detection of defects beyond limits

children.name: Expired MEL
children.definition: An event related to flight with or detection of an expired MEL

children.name: Incorrect MEL
children.definition: An event related to flight with or detection of an incorrect MEL

children.name: Incorrect part
children.definition: An event related to installation or detection of an incorrect part

children.name: Life expired component
children.definition: An event related to a life expired component

children.name: Incorrect configuration
children.definition: An event related to an incorrect configuration

children.name: Unapproved repair
children.definition: An event involving or detection of an unapproved repair

children.name: Airworthiness limitation non-compliance
children.definition: An event involving a breach of airworthiness limitation

children.name: Other
children.definition: An event related to Continuing Airworthiness Management not listed elsewhere

children.name: Documentation/Records
children.definition: An event related to inadequate or insufficient documentation/records

children.name: Aircraft operated in non-compliant state
children.definition: An event involving operation of an aircraft, when it was non-compliant

children.name: Time expired part on board aircraft
Defect deferral error by vendor (MEL/CDL etc.)
Facilities
children.definition: Building issues, rented building issues, contracted services for facilities (fire extinguishers etc.). Ensure a CRE ticket is raised and recorded in occurrence.

children.name: IT systems
children.definition: Computer hardware, software or application issues that impact Tech Ops Operations.

children.name: Manpower/Workload
children.definition: Insufficient level of manpower scheduled for bases or work required or inability to reduce/defer workloads

children.name: Occupational health and safety/personnel protective equipment
children.definition: Any Occupational Health and Safetyissues not taken by OSH team, hazards such as spills etc., and any instance of no PPE available or being incorrectly used

children.name: On-time performance (OTP) - time pressure
children.definition: Time pressure, insufficient time to complete scheduled work (daily check, serivce check, PDSC or transit check etc.)

children.name: Parts, Materials, Procurement and Shipping
children.definition: Errors during issuance and return of parts to/from stores, shipping issues, incorrectly stored components or material and issues with purchase of items

children.name: Tooling
children.definition: Lack/availability of tooling, incorrect tooling, calibration issues, tooling serviceability issues and poor handling of tools

children.name: Aircraft engine run up
children.definition: Not following Technical Ops Standards Practices  for running aircraft engines the various fleet types

children.name: Aircraft movements
children.definition: Not following Technical Ops Standards Practices  for taxiing or towing aircraft

children.name: Aircraft parking
children.definition: Not following Technical Ops Standards Practices  for parking aircraft (chocks, engine covers, probe covers etc.)

children.name: Aircraft restoration
children.definition: Not following Technical Ops Standards Practices  for completing aircraft restorations correctly after maintenance

children.name: Cold weather operations
children.definition: Not following Technical Ops Standards Practicess for cold weather operations procedures

children.name: Flight delayed
children.definition: Not following Technical Ops Standards Practices resulting in a delay to operational flight

children.name: Interactions/Teamwork
children.definition: Tech Ops members does not act in a professional and courteous manner with other team members, other internal departments or external vendors

children.name: Unable to follow standards
children.definition: Issue occurs that did not allow standards to be adhered to

children.name: standards issues
children.definition: If a gap is identified that should have a process or standard, but one does not exist or standard issue cannot be defined

children.name: Uniform appearance
children.definition: Issue with department member uniform or issues relating to uniforms

children.name: Technician/Mechanic English
children.definition: Poor understanding and usage of the English language displayed by maintenance staff

children.name: Underspeed
children.definition: Aircraft speed degraded below normal flight envelope/minimum selectable speed

children.name: Overspeed
children.definition: Aicraft speed accelerated above /maximum selectable speed/normal flight envelope

children.name: Max operating altitude
children.definition: Aircraft operated above maximum operating altitude

children.name: Flaps extended above maximum flaps operating altitude
children.definition: Aircraft flaps operated/selected above maximum operating altitude

children.name: Aircraft speed in exceedance of flap/slat speed limit
children.definition: Aicraft speed accelerates above /maximum flap/slat speed

children.name: Landing gear speed exceedance
children.definition: An event involving exceedance of the maximum airspeed permitted on the aircraft

children.name: VMO/MMO exceedance
